homeCare: Rest as needed, keep a record of symptoms, and maintain normal hydration and nutrition when medically appropriate.
precautions: Do not use leftover prescription medicines, antibiotics, steroids, or unreviewed herbal products.
Ask a licensed clinician or pharmacist before using medicine for a child, during pregnancy, or with an existing medical condition.
whenToSeekCare: Contact a healthcare professional if symptoms are severe, persistent, recurrent, worsening, or interfering with normal activities.
emergencyWarningSigns: Trouble breathing or inability to speak normally because of breathlessness
Fainting, inability to wake, sudden confusion, or seizure
Blue, gray, or very pale lips or skin
Heavy bleeding, coughing blood, or vomiting blood

homeCare: For a mild fever without concerning symptoms, rest, drink fluids, and avoid excessive clothing or blankets.
precautions: Fever guidance differs for infants, children, pregnancy, older adults, and people with weakened immunity or serious chronic illness.
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical advice for a persistent or worsening fever, dehydration, a new rash, painful urination, or other concerning symptoms.
emergencyWarningSigns: Fever with difficulty breathing, blue lips, severe headache, stiff neck, confusion, inability to wake, or seizure

homeCare: Drink water when medically appropriate and avoid smoke or other known airway irritants.
precautions: Ask a clinician before giving over-the-counter cough medicine to a young child.
whenToSeekCare: Contact a healthcare professional for a cough that persists, produces blood, occurs with fever, or is rapidly worsening.
emergencyWarningSigns: Cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, facial or throat swelling, or difficulty swallowing

clinicalReview.notes: Draft derived from cited public-health guidance.

precautions: Unexpected or significant breathing difficulty should not be managed with home remedies while waiting to see whether it improves.
whenToSeekCare: Contact a healthcare professional promptly for new or worsening breathlessness.
emergencyWarningSigns: Sudden or severe breathing difficulty is an emergency; contact local emergency services immediately

clinicalReview.notes: Emergency-oriented draft derived from cited guidance.

homeCare: Avoid known irritants and maintain comfortable hydration when medically appropriate.
precautions: Read combination cold-medicine labels carefully and ask a clinician or pharmacist which products are safe for you.
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical advice for facial or eye swelling, blurred vision, severe throat pain, or foul-smelling one-sided discharge.

homeCare: Rest and drink enough fluids to pass pale urine regularly when fluids are not medically restricted.
precautions: Do not use leftover antibiotics; urinary symptoms may require assessment and a urine test.
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical advice for painful urination, especially during pregnancy, in children, in men, or with recurrent symptoms.
emergencyWarningSigns: Urinary symptoms with confusion, marked drowsiness, difficulty speaking, severe back or side pain, or rapidly worsening illness

clinicalReview.notes: Draft derived from cited public-health guidance.

homeCare: Track fluid intake, urinary frequency, pain, fever, urine appearance, and other accompanying symptoms for clinical review.
precautions: Frequent urination can have many causes and should not be treated as a confirmed infection without assessment.
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical advice if urinary frequency is new, persistent, painful, occurs at night repeatedly, or is accompanied by blood in urine.
